response.text: Consumer fireworks may be discharged in the City only on Victoria Day or Canada Day, or on a day covered by a special occasions fireworks discharge permit issued by the Fire Chief [2]. If weather makes Victoria Day or Canada Day impractical or unsafe, the next day before or after is the designated day [2]. Victoria Day and Canada Day discharges must end by 11:00 p.m. [2]. Discharge on private land requires the prior written consent of the landowner, and you must have fire extinguishing equipment ready and accessible [2]. You also cannot discharge fireworks in a manner that may create a nuisance or unsafe condition [2]. A fireworks discharge permit is not required for consumer fireworks on Victoria Day or Canada Day [1]. The passages do not cover whether a special occasions permit is needed for every other day or the specific rules for your backyard beyond these conditions.

response.text: Under the current consolidated rule, a second-hand goods licensee may not transact business between 11:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. on any day other than Saturdays and days before a statutory or public holiday, where closing may be extended to midnight [2]. The Tuesday restriction therefore applies, so staying open until midnight on a Tuesday is not allowed under the consolidated text [2]. By-law 507-2026 deletes that closing-hours wording from § 545-282 for second-hand goods dealers, but it is not in force until 2026-09-30, so the old text still applies on 2026-10-28 [1]. The documents do not show whether the amendment's in-force date was later changed.
